13.0.0.en: Jeroboam made himself a priest and stood at the altar burning incense, so the Lord sent him a prophet from Judah to warn him, that he might have no excuse for persisting in his sins. God wanted to alert Jeroboam, so He sent him from Judah, that is, from His holy house, one to rebuke him for his evil. For God does not leave Himself without a witness. The name of the man of God is not mentioned, because he disobeyed God's commandment, as appears from (vv. 19, 20).

13.1.0.en: Josiah: the son of Amon king of Judah, who took the throne at the age of 8 years and walked according to the Law, and so opposed pagan worship.

13.1.1.en: The prophet stood at the altar where Jeroboam was burning incense and cried out with all boldness, calling in a loud voice against the altar built of stones, perhaps so that the heart of Jeroboam and of those around him of the people of Israel, whose hearts had become stony, might be moved and pay heed to God's words and stop persisting in their evils by worshiping idols. He did not speak to Jeroboam or to those standing around him, because they had persisted in evil, but spoke to the altar, that is, the stones, because they are better than these wicked men. And the man of God prophesied about Josiah king of Judah, about 350 years before his birth, that he would rise up and tear down the pagan altars and burn the bones of those who burn incense before them (2 Kgs 23:15-20), that is, defile these altars, because the bones of the dead in the Law of Moses defile whoever touches them, to declare that these altars are unclean in God's sight and were not able to protect the priests and those who worshiped before them from death. So he declares God's anger against these pagan altars and therefore demands that the people remove them and return to the worship of God in His Temple in Jerusalem, and if they do not remove them, there will come one who will remove them, namely King Josiah, but everyone who worshiped before these altars will be judged.

13.2.0.en: And so that the people might believe what this prophet was saying, since God's word would be fulfilled 350 years later by the hand of Josiah, he told them that God would give them a sign now so that they would believe his words, perhaps they would repent and turn back from the worship of idols, and this sign was that the altar before which Jeroboam stood would be rent and the ashes on it poured out, indicating thereby that God's word is able to shake stony hearts and scatter the defilement that has clung to them.

13.3.0.en: When King Jeroboam heard the prophet's words, he was not moved or aware of his error, but on the contrary he was enraged and left off offering the sacrifice that was on the altar, and stretched out his hand and pointed to the prophet, that they might seize him so that he might chastise him or kill him, but God defended His prophet with power, for He made Jeroboam's hand dry up, so he cried out, and all who stood there felt the power of God that was with the prophet and that cannot be resisted.

13.4.0.en: God fulfilled His word by splitting the altar into two parts and the ashes fell from it, and this sign showed God's power, so that all who stood there were afraid, but unfortunately this did not move them to repentance.

13.5.0.en: Jeroboam was afraid and alarmed when his hand dried up, and asked the man of God to intercede in prayer for him that his hand might be healed, and indeed the prophet did not become angry or desire vengeance on Jeroboam but besought the Lord, and the king's hand was restored whole as it was. Thus God called Jeroboam and those around him to repentance by four things:

13.5.1.en: 1- The prophet's prophecy about Josiah, who would remove the altars and kill their priests.

13.5.2.en: 2- The splitting of the altar and the falling of the ashes from it.

13.5.3.en: 3- God's making Jeroboam's hand dry up.

13.5.4.en: 4- The healing of Jeroboam's hand that had dried up and its return to health.

13.5.5.en: But unfortunately Jeroboam said to the prophet "Intreat the face of the LORD thy God" and did not try to repent and return to God that He might be his own God, and even after his healing he did not repent, and in this he resembles the pagan Pharaoh, who used to say to Moses, Pray to your God that He take away the plagues from us.

13.6.0.en: The king asked the man of God to come to his palace to eat and that he might reward him for the healing of his hand.

13.6.1.en: Thus by the power of God Jeroboam feared and respected the man of God and tried to honor him, and this is an attempt to influence the man of God not by threat, as he had pointed to him before to arrest him (v. 4), but by enticement, perhaps that he might change his words, and by this Jeroboam pretended to be attached to God in honoring His prophet, so that the people would not leave him and go to worship God in Jerusalem.

13.7.0.en: The man of God firmly refused the king's invitation, whatever gift he would give him, for he would not eat bread or drink water in this place, because it is a place full of evil and it is not right to be in it, or to mingle with the wicked, or to eat of what was sacrificed to idols, although this prophet was probably in need of food and drink and may not have had anything with which to buy, but his obedience to God is above everything, so here he clearly refuses everything connected with evil.

13.7.1.en: And the man of God's accepting the king's hospitality and gifts would mean his tacit approval of the king's evils, and this would be against the prophecy he had declared.

13.7.2.en: And by this the prophet obeyed God and did not return by the way he came, so that he would not be delayed by the people who saw or heard his prophecy and miracles, for he does the work of God clearly and with power and is not occupied with the people's praise and honoring of him.

13.7.3.en: Care to carry out God's commandments, and you will enjoy your sense that God is with you, and this will lift you up and occupy you away from the concerns of the world and separate you from its evils and thoughts.

13.7.4.en: (2) The error of the man of God and his being killed (vv. 11-26)

13.7.5.en: 11- Now there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father. 12- And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.

13.7.6.en: 13- And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon, The man of God's disobedience to the Lord's command 14- And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am. 15- Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread. 16- And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place: 17- For it was said to me by the word of the LORD, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest. 18- He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the LORD, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him. 19- So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water. 20- And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came unto the prophet that brought him back: 21- And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the LORD, and hast not kept the commandment which the LORD thy God commanded thee,

13.7.7.en: 22- But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the LORD did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. 23- And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back. 24- And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase. 25- And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

13.7.8.en: 26- And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the LORD: therefore the LORD hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake unto him.

13.8.0.en: There was an old prophet dwelling in Bethel, who had not himself been present at the preceding events at the pagan altar, but his sons were there, and when they returned they told him what had happened and of the man of God's refusal of the king's invitation and what he had said about the reason for his refusal, so he asked them about the way by which the man of God had departed, and they told him because they had followed him and knew the way. And this old man is a prophet of God, but because of his weakness he did not declare the voice of God in the midst of the evil led by King Jeroboam.

13.9.0.en: The old man asked his sons to prepare a donkey for him to ride, and went on the road by which the man of God had gone, and found him after some distance sitting under an oak tree, and asked him, Are you the prophet who prophesied at the altar? and he answered, Yes, so he welcomed him and invited him to return to Bethel to eat a meal in his house.

13.10.0.en: The man of God refused the old man's invitation because God had commanded him not to eat or drink in Bethel, but that he should depart by another way than the one he came by. By this the obedience of the man of God appears, but unfortunately it was a weak obedience that could be given up under pressure, as we will see in the following verses.

13.11.0.en: Oak: a huge tree with a large shade.

13.11.1.en: The old man lied to him and claimed that an angel had spoken to him, for he is also a prophet like him, and the angel asked him to take the man of God with him to his house to eat and drink. And this shows the weakness of the old prophet and his neglect of God's commandments. Perhaps out of curiosity he wanted to host the man of God, to learn from him the details of his prophecy, although he could have been content with asking him about it when he saw him under the tree. For though he is a prophet, he is deceitful and a liar and thinks of his personal aims at the expense of God. And by this he causes others to stumble, and the sin of causing stumbling is very grave in God's sight, because by it he destroys others, and therefore God's punishment for it is severe, which is certain destruction if the person does not repent of it.

13.12.0.en: The man of God was deceived by the venerable appearance of the old man, so he believed his lie and did not consult God in prayer before carrying out what contradicts God's commands, so he disobeyed God and returned with the old man to Bethel and entered his house to eat and rest.

13.12.1.en: The man of God was inclined to believe because he was hungry and in need of food and drink; thus Satan comes to us with his enticements from the point of weakness that he finds in us, but the Lord Christ gave us the example and model in the temptation on the mountain, when He refused to turn the stones into bread, exposing the tricks of Satan and his enticements. Be careful of your point of weakness and seek God before any action.

13.13.0.en: While they were eating together in the old man's house, the Lord spoke by the mouth of the old prophet. By this we see God speaking by the mouth of the old man despite his lying, for prophecy is a gift and does not indicate the godliness and righteousness of its possessor, as Balaam prophesied and blessed the people of God (Num 24) and also prophesied about Christ but loved money, so he became a stumbling block to the people of God and perished. And as Caiaphas the high priest in the days of Christ prophesied of the necessity of Christ's death for the redemption of the Jewish nation (Jn 11:51).

13.14.0.en: The old man told the man of God a true prophecy that God gave him, which was the punishment of the man of God for disobeying God's command when he returned to Bethel, that he would die and would not be buried in his city in the tomb of his fathers. Being buried with the fathers was a matter people cared about at that time, as Jacob asked to be buried with his fathers, and likewise Joseph his son (Gen 50:5, Heb 11:22).

13.15.0.en: After they finished eating and drinking, the old man prepared the donkey for the prophet of God from Judah to return on it to his homeland.

13.16.0.en: The man of God set out on the road returning, and behold a lion blocked his way and killed him, and his body remained lying on the road with the lion and the donkey standing beside it, to declare God's anger against whoever disobeys His commands. For when the man of God was fasting and bold in declaring his prophecy before the king, God kept him from the cruelty and violence of Jeroboam and even made the king fear him and try to honor him; but when he ate and cared for his own comfort and neglected God's commandments and disobeyed them, God's punishment came upon him, which was death.

13.17.0.en: At that time it happened that some people were walking on the same road and saw the body cast on the ground and the lion standing beside it without tampering with it or devouring it, so they came to the city in which the old prophet lived and told what they had seen on the road.

13.18.0.en: The news reached the ears of the old prophet, and he realized that the body must be the body of the man of God who came from Judah, who disobeyed the Lord's commandment, so He permitted the lion to kill him, in carrying out the divine punishment that he had pronounced by the tongue of the old man, since he disobeyed God's commandment.

13.18.1.en: The meaning of God's punishment of the prophet is not that He forgot his boldness and obedience in declaring the prophecy before Jeroboam; rather this punishment was to declare the necessity of the fear of God and obedience to Him before the wicked, like Jeroboam and the old man who was slack in declaring the voice of God, for if He does this to His prophets, how much more to those far from Him. This punishment is for the prophet of God because he knows God and it is not right that he disobey Him, for whoever knows more is required to do more, but his salvation in eternity is another matter, and God alone decides it.

13.18.2.en: (3) The burial of the man of God (vv. 27-34)

13.18.3.en: 27- And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled him. 28- And he went and found his carcase cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the carcase: the lion had not eaten the carcase, nor torn the ass. 29- And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.

13.18.4.en: 30- And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother! 31- And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones. 32- For the saying which he cried by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass. 33- After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became one of the priests of the high places. 34- And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.

13.19.0.en: The old man asked his sons to prepare the donkey and rode it and went on the road by which the man of God had gone, and found his body cast down and the lion and the donkey standing beside it. The lion's not devouring the body shows that it was sent from God to carry out the punishment and was not an ordinary hungry lion wanting to eat any prey. And the donkey's not fearing the lion and its standing confirms the submission of the animals to carry out God's commands, whereas the man of God did not obey His word and died.

13.20.0.en: The old man placed the body of the man of God on the donkey and went with it in sorrow to Bethel and declared his grief in the words of lament known at funerals, and then buried him, pained at his death.

13.20.1.en: Do not grieve after it is too late; this old man made the man of God stumble and deceived him and made him fall into disobeying God, and he died. Therefore do not be hasty in your words and actions, lest you cause others to stumble and destroy them, because your sorrows will not benefit them; so do not be hasty and rush into your opinions or decisions, but seek God before everything.

13.21.0.en: The old man charged his sons to bury him after his death in the tomb in which the man of God was buried, because when he saw the lion's killing him and not eating his body or tearing the donkey, he was sure of this prophet's prophecy about the destruction of the pagan altars, not only in Bethel but in all the cities of Samaria. Samaria had not yet been built at that time, because it was built by Omri many years later (ch. 16:24), and he made it the capital of the kingdom of Israel, and what is meant by the cities of Samaria is the whole kingdom of Israel, that is, the northern kingdom, and the old man's speaking of the tearing down of the altars in the cities of Samaria, which had not yet been built, confirms that he is a prophet of God and that this is a prophecy to that effect.

13.21.1.en: And the old man's charge to bury his bones beside this prophet's bones may be an indication of his repentance for his slackness and his lying to the man of God.

13.21.2.en: When you see God in the events around you and He makes His voice known to you, submit to Him and obey His commandments, to receive His blessing and power in your life.

13.22.0.en: Consecrated him: appointed him a priest by beginning the offering of a sacrifice to the idol.

13.22.1.en: It is certain that God's punishment of His prophet who came from Judah reached Jeroboam. And all these things, beginning with the prophecy at the pagan altar to the healing of his dried-up hand to the punishment of the man of God for disobeying the commandment, were all sufficient as a message from the Lord to Jeroboam to amend his ways, but unfortunately he did not benefit from the Lord's long-suffering and did not repent of his evil works, but continued to set up priests for the high places from outside the tribe of Levi, so that whoever desired the priesthood he made a priest. And these evils were the reasons for God's removing his kingdom and the destruction of his soul, for by these sins he judged himself.

13.22.2.en: And we notice in this chapter that all did not obey God, whether King Jeroboam, or the man of God, or the old man, and the only one who obeyed God was the lion. All went astray and became corrupt and wandered from God, and none remained obedient except the animals.

13.22.3.en: The death of Jeroboam and Rehoboam
